core.title: Make every identified test name a plan item that resolves
core.given: Any identified test in the repository (a test carrying a test identity), whether or not it currently names a plan target and whether or not it was recently changed
core.when: the tests and the plan are checked for traceability
core.then: The test must name a plan artifact of an accepted target kind, and that named item must resolve to an existing item in the plan.
prefer: Copy the exact plan artifact identity from the plan into the test.
When renaming or removing a plan item, update every identified test that names it in the same change.
avoid: Leaving an identified test with no named plan artifact.
Naming invented, stale, or misspelled plan ids.
Adding placeholder plan items solely so a test's named target resolves (metric gaming).
Stripping a test's identity to evade the check.
core.why: A test that names nothing, or names something absent from the plan, breaks plan-to-test closure, so the plan can no longer show which behaviour each test proves.
evidence: The stack's traceability-closure check reports no failures for identified tests.
Every identified test names a plan artifact of an accepted target kind, and that identity is found in the plan.
verification: Scope: every identified test, unconditionally (not only changed tests); an identified test with no named target fails, as does one whose named target does not resolve.
Accepted targets are the plan artifact kinds supplied by the profile; any one resolving satisfies the rule.
Disposition strict: every finding is a failure; no advisory mode, no ratchet baseline.

Out of scope: a genuinely unidentified test (carries no test identity at all) is not a finding of this rule, and neither is any file that is not a test; whether an unidentified test must carry an identity is decided elsewhere.

fires: An identified test names no plan artifact at all.
An identified test names a plan artifact id that does not exist in the plan.
An existing, unedited identified test still names a plan artifact that was previously removed or renamed in the plan.
A newly added identified test names a plan artifact whose id is misspelled.
doesNotFire: A test that is genuinely unidentified (carries no test identity at all); whether it must carry one is outside this rule.
A file that is not a test.

profileRequirements.meaning: The concrete plan artifact kinds that a test may name as its binding target; any one of them resolving satisfies the rule.
The concrete file kinds that play the unit-test role, so the check and activation know which files are tests in scope.
The concrete file kinds that play the acceptance-test role, so the check and activation know which files are tests in scope.

bunOnly.text: The atdd_traceability_closure validator reports no failures for identified Bun tests.
bunOnly.reason: Names this stack's validator id and its 'Bun test' file kind; the core states the same evidence generically.
The validator id and implementation type are realization details of this stack's checker; the core's verification describes the check generically.
The finding/validator identifier is realization-specific; the core keeps a generic traceability-closure finding class with the same needs_new_observer status.

bunOnly.text: task_term values: ["test identity", "test binding", "acceptance", "WMBT", "train", "traceability"] - the stack's plan-artifact kind names 'acceptance', 'WMBT' and 'train' are activation task terms in the Bun realization.
bunOnly.reason: Rule-specific task terms live in the core activation or the realization, never in the profile (notProfileKeys), so no artifact-kind profile key supplies them. The Bun realization restores 'acceptance', 'WMBT' and 'train' as task terms, and the core's generic 'plan artifact' term is instantiated in Bun by exactly those three terms, so it adds no trigger of its own; the Bun-instantiated task-term list equals bun.json's list exactly.

'plan acceptance, WMBT, or train' becomes plan artifacts of the accepted target kinds; the kinds come from the profile as binding-target data only, not as activation metadata.
'acceptance/WMBT/train identity' becomes the plan artifact identity; the concrete kinds come from the profile.
'no named plan acceptance, WMBT, or train' becomes no named plan artifact; kinds from the profile.
Empty in bun.json; the core adds no exceptions, so the obligation is neither weakened nor strengthened.
Generic 'traceability-closure check passes' in the core; the validator id stays in the Bun realization.
'acceptance, WMBT, or train' becomes accepted plan artifact kinds from the profile.
The existence of a realizing validator maps to the core's generic check description; the ref id is bunOnly.
Unconditional scope, the two failure modes, and the any-one-resolves semantics go to core:verification; the concrete accepted-target list comes from the profile as binding-target data.
Strict disposition (fails on every finding, no advisory mode, no ratchet baseline) is per-rule verification, not a profile key.
'bun_test' becomes the neutral test file kinds; the concrete kind is profile data; needs_new_observer status kept.
The core keeps a generic traceability-closure finding fact with needs_new_observer; the exact validator/finding id is bunOnly.

'test identity', 'test binding', 'traceability' are neutral and stay in the core, joined by the generic 'plan artifact' term; llm_judged kept. 'acceptance', 'WMBT' and 'train' are the stack's plan-artifact kind names acting as rule-specific task terms, which per notProfileKeys live in the core activation or the realization, so they are restored in bunOnly and carried by no profile key (roles.plan_artifact.kinds supplies binding-target kinds only, not task-term mappings). The Bun realization instantiates the generic 'plan artifact' term as exactly those three terms, so the Bun-instantiated task-term list equals bun.json's list and no extra trigger is added.

neutralityNotes: The core is fully neutral: 'Bun test' becomes the test roles with their file kinds supplied by the profile, and the accepted target kinds 'acceptance, WMBT, train' are carried by roles.plan_artifact.kinds as binding-target data, so the Bun profile instantiates the exact same obligation (name one accepted plan artifact that resolves). Rule-specific task terms are never profile data: the neutral terms 'test identity', 'test binding', 'traceability' and the generic 'plan artifact' stay in the core activation, while the stack's kind-name terms 'acceptance', 'WMBT', 'train' are restored in the Bun realization, where the generic 'plan artifact' term is instantiated by exactly those three and adds no trigger of its own, making the Bun-instantiated task-term list identical to bun.json's. The validator/finding identifier atdd_traceability_closure stays in the Bun realization. Two things could not be made concrete in the core because bun.json does not state them: how a named identity is resolved against the plan (a realization would take this from roots.plan, layout.plan_item and urn.declaration) and the concrete syntax by which a test carries its identity (urn.binding.<artifact> in a realization); the core only requires that the test name a target that resolves, exactly as bun.json does. 'Identified test' (a test carrying a test identity) is kept as a judged notion with the same observability labels as the Bun sidecar.
